correctness.rationale: In K_{n1,...,nr} selected set S, each omitted vertex of part i has t-s_i selected neighbors. The requirement exactly one implies t-s_i=1 in every unfilled part. If two parts unfilled then t<=2; proper 1-fair sets are universal singleton vertices in r>=3, cross-shore pairs in a nonstar K_{a,b}, or center-containing sets in a star. Thus complete and nonstar bipartite graphs admit N singleton fair-coalition blocks, r>=3 noncomplete has exactly 2 blocks, and nontrivial stars admit none. The all-vertex set qualifies vacuously. Independent literal fair coalition partition enumeration checked all 37 unordered multipartite profiles of orders 2..7; infinite theorem rests on the combinatorial proof.
